key_insight: In CFD predictions at L/D = 5, sharp-edged inlets showed strong cavitation above a 0.2 MPa pressure drop and hydraulic flip at 0.59 MPa, while chamfered inlets showed cavitation inception above 0.2 MPa.
engineering_relevance: Inlet geometry and orifice length-to-diameter ratio are important design variables for managing injector cavitation and flow behavior.
method: CFD of water flow through sharp-edged and chamfered single-liquid injector inlets.
k–ω SST turbulence model coupled with Zwart–Gerber–Belamri cavitation modeling and VOF.
Pressure drops of 0.07–0.59 MPa and orifice L/D ratios of 2, 5, and 10.
evidence_signal: Predicted volumetric flow rates were validated against existing experiments for both inlet types, and the sharp-edged L/D = 5 hydraulic flip agreed with prior experimental findings.
watch_item: The abstract reports no validation error metrics; flow-rate agreement alone does not establish accuracy of local vapor distributions.
paper_title: Numerical Study of Flow and Cavitation in Single-Liquid Injectors with Sharp-Edged and Chamfered Orifice Inlets
